newsitem.title: USA: FORD CEO SEES NO SLUMP IN U.S. VEHICLE SALES.
newsitem.headline: FORD CEO SEES NO SLUMP IN U.S. VEHICLE SALES.

text.p: Ford Motor Co Chief Executive Alex Trotman sees total U.S. vehicle sales of at least 15.5 million a year through 2000, even though the industry has had several robust years in a row, he said on Wednesday.
"There's room, like we've demonstrated in the last four years, for another 15 and a half new ones every year," Trotman told reporters at the University of Michigan auto conference in Traverse City.
Trotman also said Ford's cost-cutting and restructuring moves were paying off in both Europe and South America.
Ford had forecast its European operations would break even in 1997. Trotman said at a news conference that it now appeared that the operations would "do better than break even."
In South America, Trotman said Ford's projected losses will be less than previously thought, possibly down to about $300 million from $642 million in 1996.

The Brazilian market could reach two million units in 1997, Trotman said, two years ahead of when analysts had forecast it would move to that level. Ford's share of the market is between 14 percent and 15 percent, nearly doubling from a year ago.
"We're sold out of everything. We have no inventory-zero," Trotman said.
